# Mind map: the worked example's companion

The companion of the example `mindmap.atd`, in the shape of the companions under `definitions/diagrams/`, cut down to show how a trace reads it (ATD §2.5). Its one gap section lists two items; `mindmap.trace.json` names, for each, the part of the description that states it or the host's concern it is.

## 1. What DISL still lacks for this type

### Sibling naming

A new node is named `Node`, and when a sibling already has that name, `Node 2`, `Node 3` and so on: the first free number among its siblings.

### Images in nodes

A node may hold an image that Freeplane drew from a file; the image itself is drawn by the host.
